meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept.

rules.statement: A D20 test succeeds when the d20 roll plus relevant modifiers meets or exceeds its target. Ability checks and saves use a Difficulty Class; attacks use Armor Class.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — D20 Tests (pp. 6–7) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single roll against a fixed target; a world can adjust target-setting to make challenges more or less demanding, reflecting their circumstances.

rules.statement: Advantage or disadvantage adds a second d20 and uses the higher or lower result respectively. Multiple instances do not add more dice, and having both cancels them to one die.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — Advantage/Disadvantage (pp. 7–8) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one extra die with cancellation; a world can change how situational benefits combine, representing whether circumstances compound or offset.

rules.statement: A creature can apply its proficiency bonus only once to a roll, though a rule may multiply or divide that bonus; it can be multiplied once and divided once.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — Proficiency (p. 8) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one proficiency contribution; a world can tune its scale, with training and specialization determining the bonus.

rules.statement: A creature can take one action at a time, and it may take only one bonus action on its turn when a feature grants one. After taking a reaction, it cannot take another until the start of its next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions (pp. 9–10) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one action, one granted bonus action, and one reaction per round interval; a world can relax these limits at the cost of faster, more complex turns.

rules.statement: A successful search for a hidden object requires searching near its location; searching elsewhere cannot reveal it regardless of the check result.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — Finding Hidden Objects (p. 12) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring proximity and a successful perception check; a world can allow remote detection, but that requires an exceptional sensing capability.

rules.statement: Outside combat, fast travel covers 400 feet per minute, 4 miles per hour, or 30 miles per day and imposes disadvantage on Perception, Survival, and Stealth checks. Normal travel covers 300 feet, 3 miles, or 24 miles at those intervals and hinders Stealth; slow travel covers 200 feet, 2 miles, or 18 miles and grants advantage on Perception and Survival.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — Travel Pace (p. 12) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the three stated paces and their observation tradeoffs; a world can change travel distances or checks to reflect terrain and urgency.

rules.statement: A combat round represents about 6 seconds, and participants take turns in initiative order; initiative is determined by Dexterity checks at combat’s start, with surprised combatants rolling at disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — The Order of Combat (p. 13) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to six-second rounds and fixed initiative order; a world can alter round length or surprise handling to change the pace and consequences of combat.

rules.statement: A creature starts with base Armor Class equal to 10 plus its Dexterity modifier. If multiple features offer different base calculations, only one can apply at a time.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game — Armor Class (p. 7) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Dexterity-based defense formula; a world can offer alternative formulas, but each creature must choose only one.

rules.statement: Each foot moved through Difficult Terrain costs 1 extra foot, even when several features in the same space qualify. A creature can split its movement around an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction on its turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Difficult Terrain; Breaking Up Your Move (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to doubling movement cost in difficult spaces while allowing movement to be split; a world can change which surfaces qualify or the added cost to reflect how hazardous or obstructed travel is.

rules.statement: On its turn, a creature can give itself the Prone condition without spending an action or movement, unless its Speed is 0. It can pass through an ally’s space, an incapacitated creature’s space, a Tiny creature’s space, or a creature at least two size categories larger or smaller; other creature spaces usually cost extra movement, and a creature cannot willingly end its move sharing a space.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dropping Prone; Moving around Other Creatures (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to free voluntary prone movement and restricted passage through occupied spaces; a world can tighten these permissions to make positioning more consequential.

rules.statement: Half Cover grants +2 to AC and Dexterity saves, while Three-Quarters Cover grants +5; Total Cover prevents direct targeting. Cover applies only when it lies between the source of an attack or effect and its target, and only the best applicable degree counts.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three cover grades with only the strongest applying; a world can change the bonuses or which effects cover blocks to reflect how protective obstacles are.

rules.statement: A ranged attack beyond its normal range has Disadvantage, if it is within its long range, and cannot target beyond long range. A ranged attack roll also has Disadvantage when made within 5 feet of a seeing, non-incapacitated enemy.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reduced accuracy at long range and in close combat; a world can alter the distance limits or penalty to model different weapons and combat styles.

rules.statement: A visible creature provokes an Opportunity Attack when it leaves an attacker’s reach: the attacker spends a Reaction to make one melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike immediately before it leaves. Disengaging avoids this, as do teleportation and movement imposed without using the mover’s movement, action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one reaction-based melee strike when a foe leaves reach; a world can change what movement provokes it or what defenses evade it to tune the danger of disengaging.

rules.statement: Resistance halves damage of its type, Vulnerability doubles it, and multiple instances of either do not stack. Apply bonuses, penalties, and multipliers first, Resistance second, and Vulnerability third; Immunity prevents damage of a type or prevents a condition from affecting its bearer.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Resistance and Vulnerability; Immunity (p. 17) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one halving or doubling adjustment in the stated order, with immunity negating the listed effect; a world can change these magnitudes or ordering to define how defenses interact.

rules.statement: A creature at 0 Hit Points that has not died outright becomes Unconscious and makes a Death Saving Throw at the start of each of its turns. A d20 result of 10 or higher is a success; three successes make it Stable, while three failures kill it, and a 1 causes two failures while a 20 restores 1 Hit Point.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Falling Unconscious; Death Saving Throws (pp. 17–18) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a three-success/three-failure death track with specified critical results; a world can make recovery easier or harder by changing thresholds, counts, or stabilization.

rules.statement: At 0 Hit Points, any damage causes a Death Saving Throw failure, or two failures if the damage is a Critical Hit; damage at least equal to the creature’s Hit Point maximum kills it. A Stable creature remains Unconscious without making these throws, but damage ends its stability; if unhealed, it regains 1 Hit Point after 1d4 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Death Saving Throws; Stabilizing a Character (p. 18) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to worsening death saves when damage lands and slow natural recovery after stabilization; a world can make the dying more resilient or more fragile by changing these triggers and delay.

rules.statement: For a multiclass spellcaster, add all levels in spellcasting classes and half the levels in paladin or ranger, rounding down, to determine spell slots. A slot can cast a prepared spell of a lower level, and a spell’s higher-slot enhancement still applies; Pact Magic slots can also cast prepared Spellcasting-class spells, and Spellcasting slots can cast prepared warlock spells.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to combining class levels by the table and allow cross-use of slots; worlds can restrict that exchange to separate traditions, since each tradition normally has its own source.

rules.statement: A barbarian can enter Rage as a Bonus Action if not wearing Heavy armor. It grants resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, Strength-check and Strength-save Advantage, and bonus damage on Strength-based attacks; it prevents spellcasting and Concentration. It lasts until the end of the next turn, can be extended by attacking, forcing a save, or spending a Bonus Action, and can last at most 10 minutes; Heavy armor or Incapacitation ends it early.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short-lived combat state with limited uses and recovery through rest; a world can make the state harder to sustain, because maintaining it requires continued aggression or attention.

rules.statement: While Rage is active, a Berserker using Reckless Attack adds damage to the first target hit each turn, rolling a number of d6s equal to the Rage Damage bonus. Rage also makes the Berserker immune to Charmed and Frightened, and removes either condition when Rage begins.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Path of the Berserker, pp. 30–31 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fury improving attacks and suppressing fear or charm only while Rage lasts; a world can make the benefit exact greater damage, with the cost of entering the same uncontrolled combat state.

rules.statement: Bardic Inspiration gives a creature within 60 feet that can see or hear the Bard one inspiration die, which it may add to a failed d20 test within the next hour. A creature can hold only one such die; the Bard has uses equal to Charisma modifier, at least one, and regains them on a Long Rest. The die advances from d6 to d8 at level 5, d10 at level 10, and d12 at level 15.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one temporary aid token per recipient, usable to improve a failed test; a world can vary its die and recovery schedule, since the Bard’s capacity is limited by Charisma and rest.

rules.statement: A Bard can spend a Reaction when they or a creature within 30 feet fails a save against Charmed or Frightened, forcing a reroll with Advantage. A Cleric can instead spend a Reaction when a visible creature within 60 feet succeeds on a damage roll, attack roll, or ability check, expend Bardic Inspiration, and subtract its die result.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Bard: Countercharm, p. 33; College of Lore: Cutting Words, p. 35 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reaction-based interference with a limited resource for the more potent subtraction; worlds can narrow which effects can be disrupted, because the response must be timely and visible.

rules.statement: A Cleric can spend one of two Channel Divinity uses to restore a creature’s Hit Points, or make it save against equal radiant or necrotic damage; the amount is 1d8 plus Wisdom modifier, gaining another d8 at levels 7, 13, and 18. Alternatively, chosen Undead within 30 feet that fail a Wisdom save become Frightened and Incapacitated for 1 minute and flee; damage, Cleric Incapacitation, or the Cleric’s death ends this effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cleric: Channel Divinity, p. 37 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited-use divine resource that can heal or repel nearby Undead; a world can change which divine effects it fuels, with uses restored through short or long rest.

rules.statement: A Cleric can call on divine intervention to cast a Cleric spell of level 5 or lower without a slot or Material components, once per Long Rest. At level 20, the Cleric can choose Wish instead, but then must finish 2d4 Long Rests before using the feature again.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cleric: Divine Intervention, pp. 38 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a rare, deity-mediated casting that avoids ordinary resource costs; worlds can permit a more powerful request but impose a longer recovery, reflecting the scale of divine aid.

rules.statement: A Druid can assume a known Beast form as a Bonus Action, for a duration of half their Druid level in hours. The form ends early if the Druid uses Wild Shape again, becomes Incapacitated, dies, or chooses to leave it as a Bonus Action; the Druid has two uses, regains one after a Short Rest and all after a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 2: Wild Shape (pages 42–43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited, temporary animal transformation with two uses; a world can turn the duration or use count, reflecting how strongly nature’s power is available.

rules.statement: Wild Shape grants Temporary Hit Points equal to Druid level and replaces most game statistics with the Beast’s, while preserving specified personal traits. The Druid cannot cast spells in that form, though existing Concentration continues; equipment can fall, merge, or be worn, and merged equipment has no effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Rules While Shape-Shifted (page 43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a form that changes capabilities but preserves identity and selected traits; a world can make equipment merge or remain usable, with merged gear temporarily losing its effects.

rules.statement: A Druid can spend a spell slot or Wild Shape use to cast Find Familiar without Material components; the summoned Fey familiar disappears after the Druid’s next Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 2: Wild Companion (page 43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short-lived nature spirit summoned by spending another resource; a world can extend its stay, at the cost of limiting how often it can be called.

rules.statement: Once on each turn, a Druid with no Wild Shape uses can expend a spell slot to regain one use. The Druid can also spend a Wild Shape use to gain a level 1 spell slot, but cannot do that again until finishing a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 5: Wild Resurgence (page 43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exchanging power between two limited reserves, with a daily limit on turning shape energy into a spell slot; a world can change the exchange rate or recovery limits.

rules.statement: At level 20, a Druid can convert unexpended Wild Shape uses into one spell slot, with each use contributing 2 spell levels. This conversion can be used once per Long Rest.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting stored transformation power into spell capacity at a fixed rate; a world can change the rate, with stronger conversion consuming more reserve.

rules.statement: A Monk has Focus Points equal to Monk level and regains all spent points after a Short or Long Rest. At level 2, spending 1 point can fuel extra unarmed attacks, defensive actions, or movement options.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Monk, Level 2: Monk’s Focus (pages 50–51) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a level-scaled reserve that refreshes on rest; a world can change its size or refresh schedule, trading more frequent techniques against exhaustion of the reserve.

rules.statement: Once per turn after hitting with a Monk weapon or Unarmed Strike, a Monk can spend 1 Focus Point to force a Constitution save. Failure stuns the target until the Monk’s next turn; success instead halves its Speed for that duration and gives the next attack against it Advantage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Monk, Level 5: Stunning Strike (page 51) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a brief control effect with a save and a resource cost; a world can lengthen the effect or weaken the successful-save fallback, increasing the danger of each attempt.

rules.statement: A Monk can spend 4 Focus Points on a hit to plant imperceptible vibrations in one creature for a number of days equal to Monk level. The Monk can end them while on the same plane, forcing a Constitution save for 10d12 Force damage on failure or half damage on success; only one creature can be affected at a time, and the effect can be ended harmlessly.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warrior of the Open Hand, Level 17: Quivering Palm (page 52) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a costly delayed harm effect that requires continued access to the target’s plane; a world can extend the delay or increase the cost, while retaining the one-target limit.

rules.statement: A Paladin’s healing reserve holds Hit Points equal to five times the Paladin’s level. As a Bonus Action, the Paladin touches a creature and spends up to the remaining reserve to restore that many Hit Points; spending 5 points can instead remove Poisoned without healing.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a level-scaled healing pool that is spent on healing or poison removal; a world can change the reserve size or the fixed 5-point cleansing cost to reflect how readily restorative power is available.

rules.statement: A Paladin has two Channel Divinity uses, regains one after a Short Rest and all after a Long Rest, and gains one additional use at level 11. The Paladin chooses which available class effect to create each time; any required save uses the class’s spell save DC.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 3: Channel Divinity, page 54 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited pool refreshed partly by a short break and fully by a long one; a world can increase or reduce the pool and recovery rate, making divine manifestations more or less frequent.

rules.statement: Divine Sense, used as a Bonus Action, reveals the location and type of Celestials, Fiends, and Undead within 60 feet for 10 minutes, ending sooner if the Paladin becomes Incapacitated. It also detects consecrated or desecrated places and objects in that radius.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 60-foot, 10-minute supernatural detection with incapacitation as a break condition; a world can change the range, duration, or detectable categories to define what divine awareness can penetrate.

rules.statement: A Paladin’s protective aura extends 10 feet and is inactive while the Paladin is Incapacitated; the Paladin and allies within it add the Paladin’s Charisma modifier to saving throws, to a minimum bonus of +1. At level 18 its radius becomes 30 feet, and a creature benefits from only one Paladin’s protection aura at a time.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 6: Aura of Protection, page 55; Level 18: Aura Expansion, page 55 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 10-foot field that grants a Charisma-based defense bonus and expands to 30 feet at level 18; a world can tune its radius or bonus, with the effect representing a Paladin’s protective presence.

rules.statement: A Ranger’s Nature’s Veil grants the Invisible condition as a Bonus Action until the end of the Ranger’s next turn. It can be used a number of times equal to the Ranger’s Wisdom modifier, minimum once, and all uses return after a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 14: Nature’s Veil, page 59 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to brief self-concealment with Wisdom-scaled daily uses; a world can adjust duration or uses, making nature’s aid more or less dependable.

rules.statement: When a Rogue deals Sneak Attack damage, the Rogue can forgo Sneak Attack dice to add a Cunning Strike effect: 1d6 for Poison, Trip, or Withdraw; the Poison option requires a Poisoner’s Kit. At level 11, up to two effects can be combined by paying each cost, and level 14 adds Daze for 2d6, Knock Out for 6d6, or Obscure for 3d6.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 5: Cunning Strike; Level 11: Improved Cunning Strike; Level 14: Devious Strikes, page 63 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trading damage dice for a condition or movement effect, with larger effects costing more dice; a world can alter the menu or costs to set the balance between injury and control.

rules.statement: A Sorcerer can spend a spell slot to gain Sorcery Points equal to the slot’s level, or use a Bonus Action to turn points into one spell slot of up to level 5. Slot creation costs 2, 3, 5, 6, or 7 points for slots of levels 1 through 5 respectively, has minimum Sorcerer levels 2, 3, 5, 7, and 9, and created slots vanish after a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 2: Font of Magic, page 66 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reversible exchange between spell slots and a capped point reserve, with created slots expiring at the next Long Rest; a world can change the exchange rates or expiry to determine how flexibly innate magic can be stored.

rules.statement: A Sorcerer can use a Bonus Action to activate Innate Sorcery for 1 minute, gaining +1 to Sorcerer spell save DCs and Advantage on Sorcerer spell attack rolls. It has two uses per Long Rest; at level 7, a Sorcerer with no uses left can activate it by spending 2 Sorcery Points, and can use up to two Metamagic options on each spell while it is active.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 1: Innate Sorcery, page 65; Level 7: Sorcery Incarnate, page 66 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two one-minute boosts per Long Rest, with a 2-point fallback and enhanced Metamagic at level 7; a world can change the duration, benefits, or resource cost to set the intensity of innate surges.

rules.statement: A sorcerer can spend 1 Sorcery Point to protect up to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1) of a spell’s saving-throw targets: each chosen target succeeds automatically and takes no damage when a successful save would normally halve it. They can spend 1 point to double a spell’s range of at least 5 feet, or change Touch range to 30 feet.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing selective protection and range alteration for 1 point; a world can raise the cost or forbid a modification, reflecting scarce or tightly regulated sorcerous control.

rules.statement: For 1 Sorcery Point, a sorcerer can reroll up to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1) of a spell’s damage dice and must keep the new rolls. For 1 point, they can also double a spell’s duration if it is at least 1 minute, to a maximum of 24 hours; if it requires Concentration, they have Advantage on saves to maintain it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permitting one paid adjustment to damage or duration; a world can limit these adjustments to preserve magical reserves or keep extended effects from becoming disruptive.

rules.statement: For 2 Sorcery Points, a sorcerer can impose Disadvantage on one target’s saves against a spell. They can also spend 2 points to change an action-cast spell to a Bonus Action, but cannot do so after casting a level 1+ spell that turn or cast a level 1+ spell later that turn.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing costly precision or faster casting with the stated turn restriction; a world can increase the price or tighten the action limit to prevent burst casting.

rules.statement: A sorcerer can spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll a missed spell attack, omit its Verbal, Somatic, and ordinary Material components, or change its damage among Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, and Thunder. A point can also increase by 1 the effective level of an eligible spell that gains an additional target when cast with a higher-level slot.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one point buying a single listed casting alteration; a world can restrict the available alteration or raise its price, citing the strain of reshaping magic.

rules.statement: Warlock Pact Magic slots are all of the same level, cast Warlock spells of levels 1–5, and return after a Short or Long Rest. A one-minute rite restores expended slots up to half the warlock’s maximum, rounded up, once per Long Rest; at level 20, using that feature restores all expended Pact Magic slots.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warlock, Pact Magic and Magical Cunning, pp. 71–72 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a small pool of equally leveled slots that refreshes on a short rest, with one limited extra recovery; a world can reduce recovery to make pact magic rarer, at the cost of fewer reliable spell uses.

rules.statement: A warlock’s pact weapon bond ends if the warlock makes the feature’s Bonus Action again, the weapon is more than 5 feet away for at least 1 minute, or the warlock dies; a conjured weapon disappears when the bond ends. While bonded, the weapon can use Charisma for attack and damage rolls and deal one of three listed damage types or its normal type.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Eldritch Invocation Options: Pact of the Blade, p. 74 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a personal weapon bond that grants proficiency and keyed abilities but breaks under distance, death, or replacement; a world can make bonds harder to break, increasing the risk of losing access to the weapon.

rules.statement: A creature named in the warlock’s special book drops to 1 Hit Point instead of 0 when reduced to 0 without being killed outright. The book holds names up to the warlock’s Charisma modifier (minimum 1), the protection triggers only once before a Long Rest, and the warlock can erase a name by touching the page.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Eldritch Invocation Options: Gift of the Protectors, p. 73 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited roster of protected allies with one activation per Long Rest; a world can lower capacity or remove the rescue effect, making the protective bond less dependable.

rules.statement: When a warlock hits a creature with an attack, the warlock can try once per turn to send it through the Lower Planes. On a failed Charisma save against the warlock’s spell DC, it vanishes, takes 8d10 Psychic damage if it is not a Fiend, and is Incapacitated until the end of the warlock’s next turn before returning; the use refreshes on a Long Rest or by spending a Pact Magic slot.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fiend Patron: Hurl Through Hell, p. 76 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a save-gated, costly planar removal with a short incapacitation; a world can increase its cost or restrict eligible targets, reflecting the danger of calling on infernal realms.

rules.statement: A wizard can restore spell slots after a Short Rest by choosing slots whose combined levels are no more than half the wizard level, rounded up; no recovered slot can be level 6 or higher. The wizard can use this once per Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wizard: Arcane Recovery, p. 78 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited study-based spell recovery after a short rest; a world can lower the recovery cap, making magical reserves more dependent on long rests.

rules.statement: To cast a level 1 or higher spell, expend a spell slot of that level or higher; a Long Rest restores expended slots. A cantrip uses no slot, and a Ritual takes 10 minutes longer but uses no slot if the caster has the spell prepared.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to finite spell capacity restored by rest; a world can change slot recovery, with slower recovery making magic more costly.

rules.statement: A spell cast with a higher-level slot counts as that level, and its description may improve its effects. A caster can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell on a turn.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to higher slots scaling eligible spells and one slot-funded cast per turn; changing either dial alters burst power and resource pressure.

rules.statement: A spell requiring at least 1 minute to cast requires the Magic action on each of the caster’s turns and maintained Concentration. If Concentration breaks, the cast fails without spending a slot, and casting again requires starting over.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to interruption cancelling long casts without consuming their slot; a world can make interruption consume resources to raise the risk.

rules.statement: Spell components are requirements: a caster unable to provide any required component cannot cast the spell. Verbal casting requires an audible normal speaking voice, Somatic casting requires a free hand, and Material casting requires the listed materials or an allowed substitute.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to components as hard casting gates; a world can waive selected components, trading constraints for easier spell use.

rules.statement: A spell scroll lets a character cast its spell without a slot if the spell is on that character’s class list; use the normal casting time, but no Material components. A saving throw DC of 13 and attack bonus of +5 apply, and the scroll disintegrates after casting.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single-use item carrying a spell with fixed casting values; a world can allow reuse or broaden eligibility at the cost of scroll scarcity or control.

rules.statement: Attuning to an item requires a focused Short Rest in physical contact with it, separate from a rest used to identify it; an interruption makes the attempt fail. A creature can attune to at most three items and not to duplicate copies of one item.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three item bonds, each requiring focused time; a world can raise or lower capacity, with scarce bonds limiting access to magic.

rules.statement: Attunement ends if its prerequisites cease, the item is more than 100 feet away for at least 24 hours, its bearer dies, or another creature attunes to it. A creature can also end it with another focused Short Rest unless the item is cursed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic Items—Ending Attunement, p. 103 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to bonds breaking under the listed conditions or deliberate effort; a world can make bonds harder to break, increasing the risk of being tied to an item.

rules.statement: To craft a nonmagical item, the maker needs the required tools and proficiency, plus raw materials worth half the item’s purchase price. Crafting takes one 8-hour workday per 10 GP of price, rounded up; one other proficient character can normally halve the time by assisting.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Crafting Nonmagical Items, p. 103 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to tool-gated crafting with half-price materials and time based on price; a world can change materials, time, or assistance to tune production.

rules.statement: A spell must have a clear path to its target, and its description determines what kinds of targets it can affect. A caster may target themself unless the spell requires a hostile creature or someone other than the caster; an imperceptible spell normally gives its target no awareness of being targeted.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require a clear path and conceal imperceptible targeting by default; a world can relax either limit, at the cost of making spell defense and detection less predictable.

rules.statement: If a target cannot be affected by a spell, nothing happens to it, but a spent spell slot is not refunded. When a successful save would ordinarily negate the spell, the invalid target appears to have succeeded; otherwise the caster can tell the spell did nothing.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Keep costs spent on invalid targets by default; a world can refund them, reducing the risk of testing unknown targets.

rules.statement: A spell’s saving throw DC is 8 plus the caster’s spellcasting ability modifier and Proficiency Bonus. Its attack modifier is the spellcasting ability modifier plus Proficiency Bonus.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Saving Throws; Attack Rolls (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated formulas by default; a world can substitute different aptitude or training measures, changing how spell accuracy scales.

rules.statement: Different spells’ effects stack while their durations overlap, but repeated castings of the same spell do not stack: only the strongest applies. If equally strong castings overlap, the most recent one applies, and its duration determines when that effect ends.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the strongest same-spell effect by default; a world can allow repeated effects to accumulate, making coordinated spellcasting more powerful.

rules.statement: An antimagic aura extends 10 feet around its caster for up to 1 hour while concentration lasts. It prevents magic from being used or affecting things inside, suppresses ongoing spells there while their durations continue to run, and temporarily closes portals; artifact- or deity-created spells are exceptions, and antimagic auras do not cancel one another.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use a 10-foot magic-blocking aura with the stated exceptions by default; a world can widen it or exempt more magic, changing the reach and reliability of magical defenses.

rules.statement: A spell that requires concentration lasts only while the caster maintains it, up to its stated maximum; losing concentration ends its ongoing effects.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concentration limits simultaneous sustained effects; a world can relax the limit to enable layered magic, at the cost of greater magical stability.

rules.statement: Several spells let a caster spend a higher-level spell slot to increase damage, healing, area, or the number of creatures affected; the amount added is specified by each spell.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stronger results consume a higher-level slot; a world can change the scaling, with increased output paid for by scarcer resources.

rules.statement: Some spells allow an affected target to repeat a saving throw at the end of its turns; a success can end the spell’s effect on that target, while some spells instead require a specified number of successes or failures.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Compulsion, page 118; Contagion, page 119 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated resistance gives targets a chance to escape; a world can make effects more persistent, at the cost of reducing counterplay.

rules.statement: Spells that conjure spirits or create other sustained effects keep them for the stated duration, often requiring concentration; some let the caster move or direct the created effect on later turns.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Conjure Animals, page 118; Conjure Celestial, page 118 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: summoned effects persist only for their listed duration and may need active direction; a world can make them autonomous, at the cost of greater control risk.

rules.statement: Several spells sense specified things within a stated radius, but physical barriers can block the sense; some allow the caster to spend an action to learn more detail after detecting a presence.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Detect Poison and Disease, and Detect Thoughts, pages 123–124 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing is limited by range and listed barriers; a world can broaden what is detectable, with concealment and privacy becoming harder to maintain.

rules.statement: Some effects make a target obey or move in a directed way, but the target can resist at the outset and, for some effects, repeat its resistance after taking damage or after acting under the effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Compulsion, page 118; Dominate Beast, page 125 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control requires a failed resistance and can be broken under stated conditions; a world can make control harder to resist, at the cost of reduced agency.

rules.statement: A spell maintained by concentration lasts no longer than its stated maximum, and losing concentration ends its effects. Some effects also end when a target succeeds on repeated saves, takes a specified action, or meets another stated condition.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to effects ending at their stated duration or interruption; a world can lengthen or shorten them, with greater duration increasing the value and risk of sustained magic.

rules.statement: A higher-level spell slot can expand a spell’s targets, area, duration, or damage only where that spell says so; the stated increase applies for each slot level above the spell’s base level.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed per-slot scaling; a world can reduce or amplify it, making scarce high-level magic more or less potent.

rules.statement: A creature that succeeds on a saving throw against an effect often avoids or reduces it, but the result depends on the specific spell: it may take half damage, avoid the effect, or suffer a lesser outcome. Some targets automatically succeed, and some effects allow further saves or an action to end them.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to each spell’s stated save and consequence; a world can make resistance more or less reliable, shifting the cost of imposing powerful effects.

rules.statement: A spell can create a bounded area with specified dimensions and duration, altering movement, visibility, entry, or harm within that space; certain spells can be dispersed, dispelled, or prevented from overlapping.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Entangle, pp. 128; Fog Cloud, p. 133; Forbiddance, p. 133; Guards and Wards, pp. 137–138 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the spell’s exact area and end conditions; a world can enlarge or constrain warded territory, with larger protections requiring greater resources.

rules.statement: Some spells summon an allied creature that follows commands, acts on a stated initiative schedule, and disappears when its duration ends or it reaches 0 Hit Points. Certain summoned creatures can be replaced, dismissed, or resummoned, subject to the spell’s limits.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Find Familiar, p. 130; Find Steed, pp. 130–131; Giant Insect, pp. 135–136 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active familiar or steed where specified and to spell duration or defeat as the limit; a world can permit more companions, at the cost of looser control or greater upkeep.

rules.statement: Several spells move a target between planes or connect distant places through a portal; travel can be blocked by wards or planar rulers, and an occupied destination can force a traveler into a nearby open space or cause harm.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Etherealness, p. 128; Forbiddance, p. 133; Gate, p. 135 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated destination, duration, and ward restrictions; a world can make planar passage easier or harder, with access controlled by geography, cost, or powerful authorities.

rules.statement: Some effects bind or direct a creature’s behavior, but the spell defines the scope and escape conditions; for example, one long-lasting command can cause psychic harm when deliberately disobeyed, while other effects impose fear or distraction only temporarily.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Enthrall, p. 128; Fear, p. 130; Geas, p. 135 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the exact behavior limits and duration stated; a world can make compulsion stronger or weaker, with stronger control carrying a more severe cost or easier countermeasure.

rules.statement: A glyph can remain concealed on a surface or inside a closable object, then trigger when its creator’s chosen conditions are met; it can release an area burst or a stored spell, but moving it more than 10 feet from where it was placed breaks it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Glyph of Warding, pp. 136–137 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single trigger and the stated placement limit; a world can allow more complex triggers or longer-lasting glyphs, at the cost of greater components or risk of detection.

rules.statement: A spell can transform a creature’s body or size, but the target may resist, and the transformation can constrain movement, speech, object use, or attacks. Some transformed targets return to normal when the effect ends, while others require a separate remedy.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Enlarge/Reduce, pp. 128–129; Flesh to Stone, p. 133; Gaseous Form, pp. 134–135 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary transformation with the listed limits and reversal; a world can make bodily alteration more lasting, with increased risk of impairment or need for costly restoration.

rules.statement: A warded area gains configured hazards and deceptions; after the spell is cast on the same area daily for 365 days, its effects persist until dispelled.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bounded, configurable ward that expires; a world can make repeated daily casting permanent, at the cost of a year of upkeep.

rules.statement: A spell that creates a continuing effect can require concentration for a stated duration, and some effects end early when their trigger occurs or the caster repeats the spell.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the printed duration and ending conditions; a world can lengthen or shorten them, changing how long the caster must sustain the effect.

rules.statement: Hallow creates an area up to 60 feet in radius, cannot overlap another Hallow area, and binds a chosen extra effect; its consumed incense costs at least 1,000 GP.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one nonoverlapping area with a selected effect; a world can adjust area or price, with costly incense limiting widespread sanctification.

rules.statement: Some effects force a saving throw to resist; several restraining spells allow another save at the end of each affected creature’s turn, while damage can also end Hideous Laughter.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Hideous Laughter; Hold Monster; Hold Person (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated resistance and escape checks; a world can alter how often they recur, trading reliable control against a target’s chance to recover.

rules.statement: Imprisonment can hold a target without aging or needing food, water, or air; its caster names an observable ending trigger expected within a decade, and dispelling it requires a level 9 slot.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a long-lived prison with a specific release trigger; a world can widen the permitted trigger, while the powerful spell and costly dispelling constrain use.

rules.statement: Magic Jar sends the caster’s soul into a container and can exchange it with a Humanoid’s soul; possession has a 100-foot reach, and destruction or loss of the container can kill souls whose bodies are unavailable.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the container as the soul’s anchor; a world can change the range or destruction risk, with the caster’s bodily safety as the cost.

rules.statement: Instant Summons marks an object weighing no more than 10 pounds and no longer than 6 feet; crushing its named sapphire brings it to the caster unless another creature carries it, in which case the caster learns that creature’s identity and location.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a marked object recoverable by consuming its sapphire; a world can change the weight or distance limits, balancing convenience against the costly consumable.

rules.statement: Magic Circle can prevent selected creature types from entering or leaving a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder; teleporting entrants must first resist, and the circle can also hinder attacks and possession or mental influence.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed cylinder that can be reversed; a world can change the eligible types or duration, with consumed silver and salt limiting repeated use.

rules.statement: A creature or object that crosses the planar boundary of the extradimensional space described immediately before Mending is expelled to the nearest unoccupied space to its entry point, takes 50 Force damage, and becomes Prone.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Immediately before Mending, p. 149 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: expel boundary-crossers with a fixed penalty; a world can change the damage or landing rule because crossing the boundary is hazardous.

rules.statement: A spell that repairs an object can mend one break or tear no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, but repairing a magic item this way does not restore its magical function.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repair only small physical damage; a world can widen the repair limit, but magical function requires a separate restoration method.

rules.statement: A creature under Mind Blank is immune to Psychic damage and Charmed, cannot be sensed by emotion or alignment detection or have its thoughts read or location magically detected, and cannot be remotely observed, informed upon, or mentally controlled by any spell, even Wish, for 24 hours.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: strong mental and divinatory protection lasts 24 hours; a world can shorten that duration because the protection blocks even exceptional magic.

rules.statement: A successful Mind Spike save halves its damage, while a failed save also lets the caster know the target’s location for up to 1 hour while both remain on the same plane; the target cannot hide from that caster or benefit from invisibility against them. Higher slots add 1d8 damage per level above 2.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed defense leaves a persistent same-plane locator; a world can shorten the tracking period because it is tied to maintained concentration.

rules.statement: Modify Memory can change, erase, clarify, or implant memory of an event from the last 24 hours lasting at most 10 minutes; the target must fail a save and remain charmed and incapacitated while the caster describes the change. Higher slots extend the event’s age to 7, 30, or 365 days, or any time in the past at levels 6–9; damage or another spell interrupts the process, and Remove Curse or Greater Restoration restores the truth.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: memory alteration requires an incapacitated, receptive target and time to describe it; a world can extend the reachable past at increasing spell cost.

rules.statement: Planar Ally summons a loyal otherworldly servant, but the summoned creature can refuse service unless the caster negotiates payment; suggested payment is 100 GP per minute, 1,000 GP per hour, or 10,000 GP per day, up to 10 days, with adjustments for danger, safety, and alignment.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: aid depends on bargaining rather than automatic control; a world can adjust payment because dangerous or misaligned work costs more.

rules.statement: Planar Binding makes a Celestial, Elemental, Fey, or Fiend serve after a failed Charisma save; the creature must remain in range during the one-hour casting, and a consumed jewel worth at least 1,000 GP is required. The binding lasts 24 hours, increasing to 10, 30, 180, or 366 days with slots 6–9; a hostile servant may twist commands.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: forced service requires a costly, lengthy rite and can be adversarial; a world can extend the term by spending higher-level power.

rules.statement: Polymorph replaces a failed-save target’s statistics with those of a Beast whose Challenge Rating does not exceed the target’s, or its level if it has no Challenge Rating; the target keeps its identity and Hit Points, gains temporary Hit Points equal to the Beast’s, and cannot speak or cast spells in the new anatomy.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation is bounded by the target’s rating and temporary form vitality; a world can broaden eligible forms at the cost of weakening those limits.

rules.statement: A Prismatic Wall is a layered barrier; creatures crossing it encounter seven layers in order, each with its own damage or condition, and each layer can be destroyed only by its specified counter. It blocks specified attacks, spells, and movement effects until the relevant layer is removed.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain ordered layers and their specific counters; a world can remove layers more easily because the wall’s defense is designed to be overcome by targeted responses.

rules.statement: Resurrection can restore a creature dead for up to a century, including missing body parts, but not one that died of old age or was Undead; it returns with full Hit Points and a −4 test penalty that decreases by 1 after each Long Rest. Reviving someone dead at least 365 days also prevents the caster from casting spells and gives them Disadvantage on tests until a Long Rest.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: revival restores the whole body but burdens both revived creature and, for old deaths, caster; a world can adjust the age threshold because returning the dead strains life.

rules.statement: Scrying a creature uses its Wisdom save, modified from +5 for secondhand knowledge to −5 for extensive knowledge, and by −2 for a likeness, −4 for a possession, or −10 for a body part. A successful save prevents the effect and bars another attempt on that target for 24 hours; a failed save creates a sensor that follows the target for up to 10 minutes.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use connection and familiarity to set access; a world could make the modifiers harsher or kinder because personal links aid magical observation.

rules.statement: A warded creature is protected for up to 1 minute: attackers and harmful spellcasters must pass a Wisdom save or redirect their attack or spell, or lose it. The ward ends if its protected creature attacks, casts a spell, or deals damage, and it does not stop area effects.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require a save to attack the warded target; a world could broaden or narrow protection because the ward is broken by the beneficiary's aggression.

rules.statement: Sequestering makes an object or willing creature invisible and immune to magical detection and remote viewing until dispelled, until a chosen nearby condition occurs, or until it takes damage. A sequestered creature is unconscious, does not age, and needs no food, water, or air.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow hidden targets to evade magical detection; a world could restrict what ends the concealment because long-term suspension carries the risk of being stranded.

rules.statement: A harmful glyph can be hidden on a stationary surface or closed object, with a trigger and one of six effects. Once activated, it affects creatures in its 60-foot-radius area when it triggers, when they first enter on a turn, or when they end a turn there, at most once per creature per turn.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let a prepared mark impose a selected effect on trigger; a world could vary trigger precision or area because the glyph is costly and can be broken by moving its object.

rules.statement: Teleport carries the caster and up to eight willing creatures, or one eligible object, to a known destination on the same plane. Destination familiarity sets the chance of arrival; a mishap deals 3d10 force damage to each traveler or the object and requires another outcome roll.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make familiarity govern accuracy; a world could make travel safer or riskier because unknown destinations disrupt the journey.

rules.statement: Time Stop gives the caster 1d4 + 1 consecutive turns while no time passes for other creatures. It ends if an action or effect affects another creature or someone else's carried object, or if the caster moves more than 1,000 feet from the casting place.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Permit a short private interval of action; a world could change its length or ending triggers because interference with others breaks the temporal isolation.

rules.statement: A creature under Slow has half Speed, −2 AC and Dexterity saves, no Reactions, and can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both; its Attack action allows only one attack. A somatic spell has a 25% failure chance, and the target repeats its save at each turn's end to end the effect.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply a bundle of reduced actions and movement; a world could tune the restrictions because targets can resist again each turn.

rules.statement: A simulacrum follows its creator's commands, acts on the creator's turn, cannot gain levels or rest, and has half the original's maximum Hit Points. Restoring it requires a Long Rest, proximity within 5 feet, and components worth 100 GP per Hit Point; it melts at 0 Hit Points, and casting the spell again destroys earlier copies.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Model a loyal but limited duplicate with costly repair; a world could adjust upkeep because the copy cannot recover through ordinary rest.

rules.statement: A Concentration effect ends if its creator starts another Concentration effect, becomes incapacitated, dies, or fails a Constitution save after taking damage. The save DC is 10 or half the damage taken, whichever is higher, to a maximum of 30; the creator can also end Concentration at any time without an action.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one maintained effect at a time; a world can loosen that limit, while damage and incapacitation provide the in-world disruption.

rules.statement: A condition does not accumulate with itself: a recipient either has it or does not. Exhaustion is the exception.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single instance of each condition; a world can allow stacking, at the cost of more severe or layered impairment.

rules.statement: An area effect excludes locations where every straight line from its origin is blocked by Total Cover. If its origin is chosen unseen behind an obstruction, it appears on the creator’s near side of that obstruction.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Area of Effect, p. 177 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cover blocking area effects; a world can let effects pass through barriers, weakening the value of solid protection.

rules.statement: A creature with a damage threshold ignores an entire damage instance below the threshold; if one attack or effect meets or exceeds it, the creature takes that full instance of damage.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a per-hit threshold; a world can use lower thresholds to make large targets easier to wear down, or higher ones to make them resistant to small attacks.

rules.statement: True Polymorph changes a visible creature or an unworn, uncarried nonmagical object within 30 feet into a creature or nonmagical object for up to 1 hour of Concentration. Maintaining Concentration for the full hour makes the change last until dispelled; a creature can resist with a successful Wisdom save.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary transformation with a resistance save; a world can make a fully maintained change permanent, with dispelling as the remaining remedy.

rules.statement: Warding Bond gives a willing touched creature +1 AC, +1 to saves, and Resistance to all damage while it remains within 60 feet, but the caster takes damage whenever the target does. It ends if either creature reaches 0 HP, they separate beyond 60 feet, or the spell is cast again on either of them.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to shared protection with shared harm; a world can increase the range or protection, but the bonded caster pays the target’s damage.

rules.statement: Wish can duplicate any spell of level 8 or lower without its requirements, or produce listed reality changes. Any use other than duplicating a spell imposes unavoidable stress: until a Long Rest, each spell cast deals the caster 1d10 Necrotic damage per spell level, Strength becomes 3 for 2d4 days, and there is a 33% chance the caster can never cast Wish again.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to broad reality alteration with severe personal costs; a world can relax the costs, risking less restraint on world-changing magic.

rules.statement: A creature entering a Zone of Truth or starting its turn there makes a Charisma save; on failure, it cannot deliberately lie in the zone, and the caster knows whether it passed. The affected creature knows of the effect and may evade questions rather than answer falsely.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Zone of Truth, p. 176 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a local truth constraint resisted by a save; a world can make it harder to resist, at the cost of limiting truthful subjects’ speech.

rules.statement: A dead creature has no Hit Points and cannot regain them until magic revives it; its departed spirit knows who is attempting the revival and may refuse to return. Revival sets its current Hit Points, preserves still-running conditions, magical contagions, and curses, removes one Exhaustion level if it had any, and ends its magic-item attunements.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the spirit’s consent and carrying over ongoing afflictions; a world could make consent automatic or add a return cost, reflecting the spirit’s independence.

rules.statement: Each time a creature gains Exhaustion, its level rises by 1; at level 6 it dies. Each level subtracts 2 from D20 Tests and 5 feet from Speed; a Long Rest removes 1 level, and dehydration or malnutrition Exhaustion cannot be removed until the creature gets the required water or food.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Exhaustion, p. 181; Dehydration, p. 181; Malnutrition, p. 185 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative penalties and recovery through rest; a world could change the lethal threshold or require supplies to recover because deprivation has material causes.

rules.statement: A grapple requires a free hand or permitted body part and can hold only one creature with that part. The target can escape using an action and a successful Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the escape DC; the grappler can release it freely, and the hold ends if the grappler is incapacitated or the target moves beyond range.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Grappled and Grappling, p. 182 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one held target per grappling body part and an action to escape; a world could allow more holds or different escape costs to reflect anatomy and technique.

rules.statement: A magical illusion’s effect determines which senses or mental faculties it deceives. If it appears in a space, it has no substance or weight but can seem environmentally affected, such as casting a shadow or echoing.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sensory deception without physical substance; a world could let illusions affect more senses or interact physically, at the cost of greater power.

rules.statement: A Long Rest takes at least 8 hours, including at least 6 hours of sleep and no more than 2 hours of light activity; after finishing one, a creature must wait 16 hours to start another. It restores all Hit Points and spent Hit Point Dice, restores reduced ability scores and Hit Point maximum, and removes 1 Exhaustion level; specified features also recharge. Interruptions include initiative, a non-cantrip spell, damage, or an hour of exertion; after at least an hour of rest, an interruption grants Short Rest benefits, and resuming adds an hour per interruption.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to broad recovery after an 8-hour rest with a 16-hour interval; a world could make recovery less complete or rests harder to secure because danger and fatigue persist.

rules.statement: A prepared spell with the Ritual tag can be cast as a ritual by adding 10 minutes to its casting time; doing so uses no spell slot, but it cannot be cast at a higher level this way.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exchanging extra casting time for no slot expenditure; a world could alter the time or resource tradeoff to set how accessible ritual magic is.

rules.statement: A creature can hold its breath for 1 minute plus its Constitution modifier, with a minimum of 30 seconds. Once out of breath or choking, it gains 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each turn; when it can breathe again, all Exhaustion levels gained from suffocation are removed.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to turn-by-turn Exhaustion after a Constitution-based breath reserve; a world could change the reserve or penalty to reflect how forgiving its environment is.

rules.statement: A telepath can start or end mental contact with a creature in range without an action and need not see it. The recipient must understand a language or itself be telepathic; a non-telepath can reply mentally after contact starts. Incapacitation, leaving range, or the telepath contacting someone else prevents or ends contact.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two-way mental conversation only with a language-capable recipient and while in range; a world could permit one-way contact or broader reach at the cost of tighter limits.

rules.statement: Teleportation instantly moves the traveler without crossing intervening space, using no movement and provoking no Opportunity Attacks. Carried or worn equipment travels too, but a touched creature does not unless specified; if the destination is occupied or blocked, the traveler appears in the nearest unoccupied space of their choice.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to instantaneous travel with carried gear but no accompanying creature; a world could require a clear destination or charge movement because teleportation bypasses ordinary travel.

rules.statement: After 8 hours of travel in a day, each additional hour requires a Constitution save; the DC is 10 plus 1 for each hour beyond the eighth, and failure adds 1 Exhaustion level. A group member whose Speed is reduced to half or less forces the group to travel at a Slow pace.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Travel Pace; Slower Travelers (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exhaustion risk after 8 hours; a world can raise or lower the save DC or change the pace restriction to reflect how taxing travel is.

rules.statement: For extended special movement, hourly travel distance in miles equals Speed divided by 10; an 8-hour day is the usual basis, with Fast pace multiplying the distance by 1⅓ and Slow pace by ⅔, rounding down. Flight or movement that ignores Difficult Terrain permits Fast pace regardless of terrain; vehicles instead use their listed miles-per-hour speed and do not choose a pace.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed speed conversions and pace multipliers; adjust hours, rates, or terrain benefits to reflect the setting’s travel technology and conditions.

rules.statement: A magical contagion can be resisted through recuperation: after 3 days with no activity that interrupts a Long Rest, an infected creature makes a DC 15 Constitution save; success grants Advantage on saves against that contagion for 24 hours. Individual contagions can set their own infection routes, symptoms, and cure conditions.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magical Contagions; Rest and Recuperation (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a three-day recuperation and a 24-hour advantage window; vary the recovery period, spread route, and remedy to suit the outbreak’s origin.

rules.statement: A possessed creature with Demonic Possession makes a DC 15 Charisma save or is occupied by a bodiless demon. Each time it rolls a 1 on a D20 Test, the demon takes control; the creature saves again at the end of each later turn to regain control, and a successful DC 15 save after a Long Rest, Dispel Evil and Good, or curse-removing magic ends the effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Curses; Environmental Curses; Demonic Possession (p. 193) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to possession triggered by a natural 1 and repeated saves to regain agency; change the trigger, control duration, or removal method to represent the demon’s strength.

rules.statement: A magical contagion can have a delayed onset and specified routes of infection, then call for repeated saves to resist or end it. For example, Cackle Fever begins 1d4 days after infection, spreads to nearby Humanoids within a 10-foot Emanation on a failed DC 10 Constitution save, and ends after three successful DC 13 saves at Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magical Contagions; Cackle Fever (p. 194) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to contagion-specific incubation, proximity spread, and repeated cure saves; tune distance, DC, and immunity windows to set outbreak severity.

rules.statement: A creature that fails a DC 10 Constitution save after each hour swimming deeper than 100 feet without a Swim Speed gains 1 Exhaustion level. Extreme cold at 0°F or lower uses the same hourly save and DC, while extreme heat at 100°F or higher without drinkable water starts at DC 5 and rises by 1 each hour; relevant cold or fire Resistance or Immunity automatically succeeds.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to hourly exposure checks and Exhaustion; change thresholds, save intervals, or automatic protections to reflect local hazards and physiology.

rules.statement: Supernatural fear typically calls for a Wisdom save and uses the Frightened condition; the suggested DCs are 10, 15, and 20 for increasingly terrifying examples. The target usually repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the fear on a success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fear and Mental Stress; Fear Effects (p. 196) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an end-of-turn save and a DC scaled to terror; increase the DC or add behavior limits when the source is especially overwhelming.

rules.statement: Poisons take effect through contact with exposed skin, swallowing a full dose, inhalation, or a wound from a poisoned object. Contact and injury doses remain potent until triggered or washed off, while an inhaled cloud affects a 5-foot Cube and dissipates immediately; a creature harvesting venom spends 1d6 minutes and risks exposure on a failed DC 20 Nature check with a Poisoner’s Kit.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to four distinct delivery routes and a one-dose harvest limit; adjust exposure, persistence, and harvesting danger to regulate poison availability.

rules.statement: When two potions are mixed, roll d100: 1 destroys both and causes a 5-foot-radius blast for 4d10 Force damage; 2–8 destroys both and makes the mixture a poison; 9–15 destroys both; 16–25 destroys one; 26–35 halves both effects and durations, or destroys a potion with neither; 36–90 leaves both normal; 91–99 doubles one potion’s numerical effects and duration, or leaves both normal if neither can be doubled; 100 makes one potion’s simplest or most entertaining effect permanent. For more than two potions, roll again for each additional potion, combining results.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed d100 outcomes; a world can change their odds because potion ingredients interact unpredictably.

rules.statement: Unless an item says otherwise, a ring’s magic works only while it is worn on a finger or similar digit.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a suitable digit; a world can broaden eligible body parts to account for different anatomy.

rules.statement: A scroll is consumed when its magic is invoked: its writing disappears or the scroll crumbles. A creature able to understand a written language can read and try to activate one unless its description says otherwise.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one use per scroll; a world can permit exceptions because particular scroll magic may resist consumption.

rules.statement: Item spells are normally cast at the lowest possible spell and caster level, use no spell slot or components, and use their normal casting time, range, and duration; the user concentrates if required. An item can specify exceptions, and may require the user’s spellcasting ability; without one, the modifier is +0 and proficiency still applies.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Activating a Magic Item—Spells Cast from Items, p. 206 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to minimum-level, slot-free casting; a world can make item descriptions override these defaults because items may embody specialized magic.

rules.statement: Some items spend charges to activate properties. Identify reveals how many charges remain; an attuned creature knows the remaining and regained charges. A recharge tied to an event such as dawn is timed by the GM if that event does not occur in the item’s current world or plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Activating a Magic Item—Charges and “The Next Dawn,” p. 206 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the item’s stated charge and recharge schedule; a world can substitute a local recharge time when its specified event is absent.

rules.statement: Most identification methods, including Identify, do not reveal a magic item’s curse. Attunement to a cursed item cannot be ended voluntarily until the curse is broken.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealed curses that persist through unequipping; a world can make detection easier because curses may be less secretive.

rules.statement: Crafting a magic item requires Arcana proficiency, the listed proficient tool, and any spells the item casts prepared on every crafting day. Work 8 hours per day; base time and cost are 5 days/50 GP for common, 10/200 for uncommon, 50/2,000 for rare, 125/20,000 for very rare, and 250/100,000 for legendary items. Consumables other than Spell Scrolls take and cost half as much; assistants divide the time, and unavailable materials require waiting at least 7 days before checking again.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Crafting Magic Items—Time and Cost, p. 207 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed training, tool, time, and material gates; a world can alter availability because suitable materials may be scarce.

rules.statement: A sentient item can object when its bearer acts against its alignment or purpose: the bearer makes a Charisma save against DC 12 plus the item’s Charisma modifier. On failure, the item can demand a change in conduct; if refused, it can block attunement, suppress activated properties, or try to control the bearer. That control uses the same save DC and, on failure, charms the bearer for 1d12 hours; damage allows another save to end it, and the item cannot try again until the next dawn.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the item’s GM-controlled demands and stated save; a world can make sentient items more or less forceful because their relationship with bearers varies.

rules.statement: A worn or held magic item can grant a continuing benefit, but some benefits work only while worn, held, or attuned; particular powers also require an action or a command.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to powers tied to an item and its use conditions; a world can loosen or tighten attunement and action requirements, with access to the item as the in-world limit.

rules.statement: Some item powers spend charges, regain a stated amount at dawn, and cannot be used again until a specified time; single-use objects may lose their magic when activated.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to finite charges with the stated recovery schedule; a world can adjust reserves or recharge rates, with scarcity controlling repeated use.

rules.statement: An item can summon a creature that follows commands for a limited duration, then disappears or returns to its object; some summoned creatures act independently or may disobey.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 220–223, Efreeti Bottle; Elemental Gem; Figurine of Wondrous Power (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a commanded companion with a duration and dismissal condition; a world can alter obedience, duration, or recovery, with risk and upkeep limiting the bond.

rules.statement: Some items impose a condition or control effect on a creature after a failed saving throw; the effect may allow repeat saves, end on a specified event, or persist while a cursed item is worn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 218–220, Dragon Orb; Dust of Sneezing and Choking (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bounded condition with its stated escape route; a world can change the save or duration, with loss of agency as the cost.

rules.statement: A number of effects alter space: they can bar extradimensional movement, place a target elsewhere, or open a route between planes; these effects differ in which routes they block or permit.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 218, 220, 224–225, Dimensional Shackles; Cubic Gate; Energy Bow; Handy Haversack (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the specific routes or storage limits listed for each effect; a world can broaden access, with confinement, capacity, or dangerous destinations as constraints.

rules.statement: An illusion can conceal or misrepresent a creature or object, but physical interaction or close examination may reveal it; some illusions end when their source moves or is dismissed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 217–218, Cloak of Displacement; Deck of Illusions; page 224, Glamoured Studded Leather (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealment that fails under the stated inspection or interaction; a world can make detection harder or easier, with exposure to scrutiny as the limitation.

rules.statement: A creature can be transformed into another form by an item, sometimes retaining selected mental abilities; such transformations have a fixed duration or end when the item is no longer used.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 216, Cloak of the Bat; pages 222–223, Figurine of Wondrous Power (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary form with only expressly retained traits; a world can vary duration or retained abilities, with dependence on the item as the cost.

rules.statement: An item can create a bounded area or barrier, or change conditions within an area, with its size and duration set by the item’s effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 216–221, Web; Cube of Force; Eversmoking Bottle; Feather Tokens (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed area and duration; a world can turn the area or persistence dial, with charges, visibility, or environmental conditions limiting use.

rules.statement: Some item effects end when the user takes a specified action, stops meeting a condition, takes damage, or reaches a stated time limit.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated ending trigger; a world can make effects more stable or fragile, with damage, movement, or time serving as the balancing cost.

rules.statement: An Ioun Stone activated by tossing it into orbit grants its benefit while orbiting 1d3 feet from the user; no more than three stones can orbit one user at once. The stones count as worn objects and evade collisions and attempts to grab or strike them.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limit of three orbiting stones; a world can raise or lower the cap, with greater capacity making stacked benefits easier to obtain.

rules.statement: A Mysterious Deck user declares how many cards to draw, then draws them randomly, no more than 1 hour apart. Undrawn declared cards fly out and take effect together; each drawn card vanishes, then returns to the deck except the Fool and Jester.
